domain_entities.name: LeaveRequest
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee's application for leave. Tracks the full lifecycle from draft through submission, approval/rejection, and cancellation. The status field drives all state transitions.
lifecycle_states: DRAFT: Initial state when an employee begins but has not yet submitted a leave application. Editable by the employee. No balance impact.
SUBMITTED: Employee has submitted the request for manager review. No longer editable by the employee. Awaiting manager action.
APPROVED: Manager has approved the request. Balance is deducted. The leave is confirmed and visible on calendars.
REJECTED: Manager has rejected the request with a reason. No balance impact. Terminal state (cannot be resubmitted; a new request must be created).

CANCELLED: The request has been cancelled. Can be reached from DRAFT (employee discards), SUBMITTED (employee withdraws), or APPROVED (employee cancels confirmed leave; balance is restored). Terminal state.

domain_entities.name: LeaveBalance
domain_entities.purpose: Tracks an employee's leave entitlement, usage, and remaining balance for a specific leave type within a fiscal year. `pendingDays` captures days tied to SUBMITTED (not yet approved) requests. `remainingDays = totalEntitlement + carriedForward - usedDays - pendingDays`. Mutated on approval (usedDays += days, pendingDays -= days) and on cancellation of approved leave (usedDays -= days).
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE: The balance record for the current fiscal year. Accruals and deductions apply.
CLOSED: The fiscal year has ended. Balances are frozen; no further deductions or accruals. Carried-forward days may be transferred to the next year's ACTIVE record.

domain_entities.name: LeaveType
domain_entities.purpose: Catalog of leave categories available in the system (annual, sick, emergency, unpaid, maternity, paternity). Each LeaveType is referenced by LeavePolicy and LeaveRequest. The code is the stable identifier used in business logic.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE: The leave type is available for new requests.
INACTIVE: The leave type is disabled; no new requests can be created against it. Existing requests are unaffected.

domain_entities.name: LeavePolicy
domain_entities.purpose: Defines the rules governing a specific leave type. Each policy specifies entitlement, accrual behaviour, notice requirements, and approval rules. Referenced by LeaveBalance to determine entitlements and by LeaveRequest validation to enforce constraints (e.g. minimum notice, max consecutive days).
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE: The policy is in effect. All new leave requests of the associated type are validated against this policy.
INACTIVE: The policy is retired. No new requests are validated against it. Existing balances and approved requests are unaffected.

business_rules: BR-001 — LeaveRequest state transitions: DRAFT → SUBMITTED (employee submits); SUBMITTED → APPROVED (manager approves); SUBMITTED → REJECTED (manager rejects); DRAFT → CANCELLED (employee discards); SUBMITTED → CANCELLED (employee withdraws); APPROVED → CANCELLED (employee cancels confirmed leave). REJECTED and CANCELLED are terminal states. No transition can skip states.

BR-002 — Balance deduction: When a LeaveRequest transitions to APPROVED, the corresponding LeaveBalance.usedDays is incremented by the number of working days in the request period, and pendingDays is decremented by the same amount. The balance must never go negative unless the LeavePolicy.allowNegativeBalance is true.

BR-003 — Balance restoration: When an APPROVED LeaveRequest is CANCELLED, the corresponding LeaveBalance.usedDays is decremented by the number of working days originally deducted. No restoration occurs for cancellations from DRAFT or SUBMITTED states (no balance was deducted).

BR-004 — Pending balance reservation: When a LeaveRequest transitions to SUBMITTED, the corresponding LeaveBalance.pendingDays is incremented by the number of working days in the request. This prevents double-booking. If the request is REJECTED or CANCELLED from SUBMITTED, pendingDays is decremented back.

BR-005 — Sufficient balance check: Before a LeaveRequest can transition from DRAFT to SUBMITTED, the system must verify that remainingDays (totalEntitlement + carriedForward - usedDays - pendingDays) >= the requested working days, unless the policy allows negative balance. If insufficient, the submission is rejected with a clear error.
